answer: Each identity that wants to transact in the agent economy locks a bond before it may operate, and the bond sits in escrow like a crystal weight holding the identity down. When auditors notice that several agents share the same behavior pattern, a single orchard of cloned workers swaying together in the same tide, they trigger a slashing rule that seizes the deposits and burns the duplicates. Because each clone needs its own full bond, spawning fakes costs more than they earn.
